title: Church practices like not rebaptizing may be held without binding as heresy — Cyprian
source_text: XXIV. Inde vero colligi potest quid sit respondendum adversariis, dum impugnantes sufficientiam, quam Scripturae sacrae tribuimus, objiciunt quaedam in nostris Ecclesiis teneri, & doceri, quae tamen per consequentias tam apertas & necessarias ex Scriptura non deducuntur, ut possint Christiani populi fidem obligare, nisi aliunde divina quadam authoritate fulciantur: ut ex. gr. non esse de novo baptizandos eos qui semel apud haereticos baptismum susceperunt. Etenim dogma istud, & alia nonnulla in Ecclesiis nostris tenentur quidem, & docentur, ut Scripturae consentanea, & praeterea longo usu & communi fidelium suffragio probata, quae propterea temerarium est damnare atque rejicere: nec tamen eam illis tribuimus necessitatem, ut Christianorum fidem necessario obligent, adeo ut qui aliter sentit sit e fidelium numero expungendus, & accensendus haereticis, quibus minime vellemus annumeratum Cyprianum virum sanctum & Christi martyrem, qui de baptismo haereticorum non idem sensit quod Ecclesiae nostrae.
pass_a_gloss: From this truly it can be gathered what is to be answered to adversaries when, attacking the sufficiency which we attribute to sacred Scripture, they object that certain things are held and taught in our churches which nevertheless are not deduced from Scripture by consequences so open and necessary that they can bind the faith of the Christian people unless they are propped up from elsewhere by some divine authority: as for example, that those who once received baptism among heretics are not to be baptized anew. For that dogma, and some others, are indeed held and taught in our churches as agreeable to Scripture, and moreover proved by long use and the common suffrage of the faithful, which for that reason it is rash to condemn and reject: yet we do not attribute to them such necessity that they necessarily bind the faith of Christians, so that whoever thinks otherwise is to be struck from the number of the faithful and counted among heretics — among whom we would by no means wish Cyprian numbered, a holy man and martyr of Christ, who did not sense the same about the baptism of heretics as our churches do.
pass_b_english: So we can answer adversaries who attack the sufficiency we give Scripture. They object that our churches hold and teach some things not drawn from Scripture by consequences open and necessary enough to bind the people's faith unless some other divine authority props them up — for example, that those once baptized among heretics are not to be baptized again.
That teaching, and some others, our churches do hold and teach as agreeing with Scripture, and as confirmed by long use and the common vote of the faithful. It is rash to condemn and reject them.

Yet we do not give them such necessity that they bind Christian faith as such — as if whoever thinks otherwise must be struck from the faithful and counted a heretic. We would never want Cyprian so numbered: a holy man and martyr of Christ, who did not hold the same view of heretics' baptism that our churches hold.

choices.why: Consensus of the faithful, not a ballot slogan.

rejected: newly baptized from scratch as converts only
